title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
source: canonical Longest Consecutive Sequence concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an unsorted array of integers. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive values that can be assembled from its elements, in any order: values 4, 5, 6 form a run of length 3. Duplicates count once, and an empty array has a longest run of 0.

examples.explanation: The values 1 through 5 all appear, forming a consecutive run of 5.
Every value from 1 through 9 appears at least once, and the duplicate 2 counts once.

hints: Checking membership over and over is only cheap if the container answers in constant time.
Put every value in a set. A value only needs checking when it is the start of a run, which is true exactly when value - 1 is absent.
For each run start, walk value + 1, value + 2, ... while the set contains them, and track the longest walk. Only starting from run starts keeps the total work linear.
solution: Load the values into a set for O(1) membership tests. Treat a value as a run start only when value - 1 is not in the set, then count upward while the next value exists. Every element is visited a constant number of times: O(n) time, O(n) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include an empty array, duplicates, negative values, and one long run among scattered values

visible.failNote: runs assemble values in any order
